title: Which edges of a glass cube make the outline?
description: A glass cube balanced on a corner is projected onto the floor. The board finds where the top and bottom corners land, counts the edges inside the outline, and finds the edges left for the outline. Keeko's doubt is that every edge is on the outline.
teaching_notes: One idea: a cube balanced on a corner has its top and bottom corners on one vertical line, so both land at the centre and the six edges at those corners lie inside the outline. Watch for students who put all twelve edges on the outline.

source: A glass cube balanced on a corner is projected onto the floo
video_script.why: The child counts the edges inside and on the outline of a cube balanced on a corner by finding where the top and bottom corners land.
video_script.substitution: Edges on the outline = 12 minus the edges at the top and bottom corners.
video_script.anchor: a glass cube balanced on one corner above the floor, with its outline drawn on the floor below
video_script.wrong_answer: every edge is on the outline
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks every edge is on the outline. The top corner and the bottom corner both land at the centre, so the six edges at those corners lie inside.
video_script.payoff_line: Six edges make the regular hexagon, and six run inside from its centre

final_answer.value: 6 edges make the regular hexagon and 6 run inside from its centre
final_answer.spoken: six edges make the regular hexagon, and six run inside from its centre

hold_back: Answer: 6 edges make the regular hexagon and 6 run inside from its centre
never_show: all twelve edges on the outline marked as right
maths_rules: balanced on a corner: the top corner is straight above the bottom corner, so both land at the centre of the outline
3 edges leave the top corner and 3 leave the bottom corner: 3 + 3 = 6 inside
all 12 edges project to equal lengths, so the outline is a regular hexagon
slip: every edge is on the outline, which leaves no edge inside
video_script.design: The glass cube on the stage with a light above it. Its top and bottom corners slide down to the centre of the floor outline, the six inner edges are tinted, and the six outline edges are traced.

narration: <bookmark mark='slide'/>Step one, find where the top and bottom corners land.
<bookmark mark='centre'/>They sit on one vertical line, so both land at the centre of the outline.

beats.on_screen: Inside: 3 + 3 = 6 edges run from the centre outwards

marks.inside: the six edges at the two corners are tinted and run from the centre outwards

narration: <bookmark mark='inside'/>Step two, count the edges inside. Three edges leave the top corner, and three leave the bottom corner.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Three plus three makes six, and all six run from the centre outwards.

marks.rest: the six edges that are left are traced as the outline

narration: <bookmark mark='rest'/>Step three, count the outline. The edges left are twelve minus six.
<bookmark mark='minus'/>That is six edges.

narration: <bookmark mark='equal'/>Step four, check the shape. All twelve edges project to equal lengths.
<bookmark mark='hex'/>A hexagon with six equal sides is called a regular hexagon, and that is the outline.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 6 edges make the regular hexagon and 6 run inside from its centre
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Six edges make the regular hexagon, and six run inside from its centre.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks every edge is on the outline, because the cube has twelve edges.
<bookmark mark='centre'/>But the top corner and the bottom corner both land at the centre.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Six edges start there and lie inside, so only six are left for the outline.
